Plot discrete life-contingent cash flows

Source: R/plot_contingent_cash_flow.R
plot_contingent_cash_flow.Rd

Separates contractual amounts, unconditional payment probabilities, expected cash flows and actuarial present-value contributions in editable panels. Consumes the payment-level output of apv_life_flow() without recomputing mortality, dates or interest, or an explicitly specified event table.

Usage

plot_contingent_cash_flow(
  .data,
  view = c("all", "contractual", "probability", "expected", "pv"),
  title = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  x_label = NULL,
  show_labels = TRUE,
  label_size = 3.2,
  label_digits = 2L,
  label_format = c("auto", "full", "compact"),
  currency = "",
  col_inflow = "#1B9E77",
  col_outflow = "#D95F02",
  date_labels = "%Y-%m-%d"
)

Arguments

.data

A nonempty data frame or tibble. Supply an apv_life_flow() result, or columns t, cf, probability, discount and event. Optional date supplies the horizontal calendar axis. Optional expected_cf and pv are reused after consistency checks.

view

One of "all", "contractual", "probability", "expected", or "pv". The default shows four panels with separate vertical scales.

title, subtitle

Optional plot title and subtitle.

x_label

Optional horizontal axis label.

show_labels

Logical. Show amount/probability labels, omitting text that overlaps at rendering time. All payment rows remain in the plot.

label_size

Positive text size.

label_digits

Integer between 0 and 50 for monetary labels.

label_format

Monetary notation: "auto", "full", or "compact", as in plot_cash_flow(). Probabilities/weights use separate unitless labels.

currency

Monetary prefix; never applied to probabilities or weights.

col_inflow, col_outflow

Colors for positive and negative monetary flows.

date_labels

Calendar label format for ggplot2::scale_x_date().

Value

An editable ggplot2 object. Its tibble data has one row per payment per selected measure: row, t, x, event, measure, value, plot_value and label. value retains original units; extreme monetary panels use scaled plot_value with the power of ten in the panel title.

Details

For a binary payment event \(E_j\), contractual signed amount \(C_j\), payment date \(t_j\) and deterministic discount \(d_j\), the panels show $$C_j,\quad p_j=P(E_j),\quad C_jp_j,\quad C_jp_jd_j.$$ Probabilities are unconditional relative to the common initial actuarial state, not conditional annual mortality rates. For survival payments, \(p_j={}_{t_j}p_x\). For death in \((a,b]\), \(p_j={}_ap_x-{}_bp_x={}_ap_x\,{}_{b-a}q_{x+a}\). A benefit payable at the end of that interval is discounted to its payment date, not the exact time of death. Continuous death-time benefits require a different model.

In explicit event tables, event contains "survival", "death_interval" or "certain" (the last requires probability one). Interval probabilities must be supplied; the plot never differences arbitrary rows of a stream. Rows may represent different events at the same date; probabilities are never added or netted. Coincident stems can overlap; points identify their endpoints and no payment date is moved. Negative amounts denote outflows.

For new apv_life_flow() results, contingency metadata distinguishes binary survival from a reversionary expected benefit fraction. For the latter, surv_prob is \(P(\text{all alive})+\alpha P(\text{some but not all alive})\), not generally a probability: the second panel is labeled Expected benefit fraction. Results lacking metadata use the conservative label Payment weight; no event is inferred from column names alone. Explicit tables can use event = "weighted" for such finite multipliers as well.

life_contract() stores a specification, and insurance_x()/annuity_x() return aggregate values rather than payment schedules. These objects cannot be plotted directly: supply an explicit payment table instead. The plot does not expand contracts or reevaluate actuarial assumptions.

All required numeric values must be finite, with nonnegative t and discount, and probabilities in \([0,1]\) for binary events. Missing or inconsistent rows are rejected, never silently removed. Supplied expected amounts and PVs must agree with the identities to relative tolerance 1e-10; they are retained, not replaced. The plot ignores cached APV/cumulative attributes and sums the displayed contributions. Calendar dates and stored t are retained; in particular apv_life_flow() uses actual days/365.25. All rows must share a valuation origin and monetary unit.

See also

plot_cash_flow(), apv_life_flow(), life_contract(), insurance_x(), annuity_x()

Examples

lt <- tibble::tibble(x = 60:64, lx = c(1000, 800, 600, 300, 0))
apv_life_flow(lt, ages = 60, t = 1:3, cf = rep(1200, 3), i = 0.04) |>
  plot_contingent_cash_flow(currency = "$")


# Three-year term insurance, paid at each year-end of death.
# P(j-1 < T <= j) = (l[x+j-1] - l[x+j]) / l[x], not q[x+j-1].
death_flows <- tibble::tibble(
  t = 1:3, cf = rep(10000, 3),
  probability = c(200, 200, 300) / 1000,
  discount = 1.04^-(1:3), event = "death_interval"
)
death_flows |> plot_contingent_cash_flow(currency = "$")

death_flows |> plot_contingent_cash_flow(view = "pv") +
  ggplot2::labs(title = "Term insurance: contributions to APV")
